Smart Battery Management Systems in Solid-State Batteries: An Overview Recent advancements in battery technology have notably focused on developing Smart Battery Management Systems (SBMS) for Solid-State Batteries (SSBs), enhancing their performance and safety due to SSBs' high energy density and complexity. A Battery Management System (BMS) principally engages in gathering and analyzing battery data, developing and applying predictive models for battery states, overseeing charge and discharge processes, diagnosing faults and issuing alerts, managing temperature, maintaining cell balance, and handling communications, with the most advanced systems placing a strong emphasis on precise battery modeling and state estimation [12]. These include a dual NN fusion model by Dang et al., which combines a linear NN for parameter identification with a backpropagation NN to correlate open-circuit voltage (OCV) with SoC [17]. Sun et al. developed a Radial Basis Function Neural Network to construct model bias response surfaces in multi-cell battery packs [18]. Tong et al. introduced a load classifying NN model that enhances overfitting suppression [19]. Chemali et al. implemented a Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network, coupled with a Back-Propagation Neural Network strategy, for effective SoC estimation in Li-ion batteries [20]. Challenges and Future Research Directions 4.1Current Challenges in SBMS for SSBs / • Ionic Conductivity and Electrochemical Performance: The paper by Bielefeld et al. focused on the influence of binder and microstructure on ionic conductivity in composite cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) [28]. It emphasizes the role of electrode composition, including active material particle size and binder content, on lithium-ion transport. The study employs three-dimensional microstructure models to evaluate effective ionic conductivity and tortuosity, demonstrating that even small amounts of binder can significantly impact ion transport paths and active surface area. The research highlights the complex relationship between microstructure and electrochemical performance in ASSBs, underscoring the importance of microstructural optimization for enhancing battery performance
